last_verified_note: Each provider has its own last_verified date. Values not confirmed from official documentation are the string "unverified".

providers.name: Groq

limits.summary: Free plan: 30 RPM, 1K RPD, 8K TPM, 200K TPD on the chat models listed below. Limits apply per organization.

providers.notes: Responses API is documented as beta and lacks previous_response_id, store, truncation and stateful conversations. The docs only mention a payment method as required to upgrade to the Developer plan; they do not state whether the Free plan needs one.

providers.name: Cerebras

limits.summary: Documented as a free trial tier: 5 RPM, 30K uncached TPM, 90K total TPM, 1M tokens per hour, 1M tokens per day on gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b.

providers.notes: A verified payment method is required to activate the $5 in free credits; without it, Playground and API access stay inactive. Cerebras' own docs call this a free trial tier, so it is not a permanent no-card free plan.

providers.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini API)

limits.summary: Google does not publish numeric free-tier RPM/RPD/TPM values in its docs. Its own rate-limits page states limits depend on usage tier and instructs users to check the AI Studio dashboard, which requires sign-in and is account-specific. Confirmed absent from official docs, not merely unresearched.

providers.notes: Model IDs are those with a Free Tier price of 'Free of charge' on the pricing page. On the free tier the pricing page lists 'Used to improve our products: Yes', meaning free-tier content may be used by Google to improve its products; the paid tier lists No. The billing page says new accounts begin on the Free Tier and that upgrading means linking a billing account and prepaying at least $5; it does not state outright whether the free tier needs a card. Free-tier availability and limits vary by model and can change.

providers.name: OpenRouter

limits.summary: Free model variants (IDs ending in :free): 20 requests per minute. 50 requests per day if you have purchased less than $10 in credits (lifetime); 1,000 requests per day once you have purchased $10 or more in credits (lifetime). Confirmed from OpenRouter's own API reference.

providers.notes: Free variants change often; list them with GET /api/v1/models and filter for IDs ending in :free. OpenRouter documents a Claude Code setup using the Anthropic-format base URL https://openrouter.ai/api. Anthropic does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through a gateway (see docs/guides/claude-code.md).

providers.name: Mistral AI

limits.summary: Mistral's docs state a free API tier exists with 'restrictive rate limits' but do not publish the numeric values; they direct users to console.mistral.ai/limits/, which requires an account login and is workspace-specific. Confirmed absent from official docs.

providers.notes: The model ID is the example used in the API reference; which models are included in free mode is not confirmed. Docs state: free mode API access is enabled by default with no credit card required. Phone verification is not mentioned in the pages checked. The base URL is derived from the documented endpoint https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI

limits.summary: 10,000 neurons per day at no charge; limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC.

providers.notes: Requires your account ID in the base URL and an API token with Workers AI Read and Edit permissions. The model catalog lists the Llama model as @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8; the OpenAI-compatibility page uses @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct in its examples, which the catalog does not list. The Responses API is documented only for the two gpt-oss models, non-streaming. Some models (for example Moonshot Kimi, Zhipu GLM-5 and DeepSeek V4 variants) require a paid billing method.

providers.name: NVIDIA NIM (build.nvidia.com)

limits.summary: NVIDIA does not publish a fixed free-tier RPM in its official docs. A moderator on NVIDIA's own developer forum stated limits 'depend on model, use-case and the amount of current overall traffic' and declined to give a fixed figure. Developers commonly report roughly 40 RPM in forum threads, but this is not an official published number and should not be relied on.

providers.notes: Official docs give the host https://integrate.api.nvidia.com and the endpoint POST /v1/chat/completions. Model IDs are listed on each model page at build.nvidia.com. Community forum posts mention a 40 RPM default; that is not from official documentation and is not recorded as a limit here.

providers.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers

limits.summary: Free users receive $0.10 of Inference Providers credit per month, subject to change. Further use requires purchasing credits.

providers.notes: A provider can be selected by suffix, for example openai/gpt-oss-120b:groq, or a policy suffix such as :fastest or :cheapest. The token needs the 'Make calls to Inference Providers' permission. The Responses API is documented as beta. On 2026-09-26 the router's GET /v1/models listed openai/gpt-oss-120b as live on several providers and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 as live on featherless-ai and deepinfra; availability changes.

providers.name: Together AI

limits.summary: Together AI does not publish fixed per-model rate limits; its docs state limits are dynamic and scale with usage and live model capacity. Separately, its own pricing page lists one specific model, Ternary Bonsai 27B, priced at $0.00 per token for both input and output, confirmed live on together.ai/pricing. Other models on the platform are paid.

providers.notes: Only the specific model listed above is confirmed free. The rest of Together AI's catalog is paid; do not assume other model IDs are free without checking the live pricing page, since it changes.
